observations: Three photos show a white plastic tank encased in a grey/galvanized steel cage - a standard IBC (intermediate bulk container) tote, stacked among similar totes in an outdoor yard.
A blue plastic ball-valve/spigot is visible at the bottom front of the tank (photo 0, photo 1).
Embossed lettering on the plastic tank reads something like '...1000' and '250-L...' (photo 2), consistent with a common IBC size marking but not fully legible.
A red/white warning-style sticker and a barcode sticker are visible on the tank shoulder (photo 1) but text is too small/blurred to read.
The cage shows surface discoloration and light rust/wear at joints; the base pallet/skid is partly obscured by stacking.
No visible cracks, dents, or major leaks in the plastic, but dirt and staining are present on the tank surface.
Multiple other totes are stacked around it, suggesting a bulk lot or yard rather than a single controlled unit.

identity.kind: IBC tote tank (caged plastic container, appears ~1000L)

claims.claim: Suitable 'to store industrial liquids or hazardous chemicals'
claims.evidence: No certification plate, UN/DOT rating, or prior-use history visible in any photo; sticker in photo 1 is unreadable.

claims.claim: Implied capacity of 1000 litres (from embossed '1000' in photo 2)
claims.evidence: Partial embossed text in photo 2 is consistent with a 1000L IBC but not fully clear or confirmed by a full nameplate shot.

risks.risk: Unknown prior contents (could have held hazardous or corrosive chemicals affecting food/water safety)
risks.proof: Close-up of the UN/chemical hazard sticker and any manufacturer plate showing prior fill history
risks.if_unproven: priced as unknown/contaminated-risk, not suitable for sensitive liquids

risks.risk: Cage corrosion or weld damage reducing structural/load safety
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all four cage corners and base welds

risks.risk: Valve/spigot leak or crack not visible in current angle
risks.proof: Video of valve being opened/closed and water poured through

risks.risk: Tank wall micro-cracks or UV degradation (common in reused IBCs)
risks.proof: Clear daylight photos of all tank faces without cage obstruction
risks.if_unproven: priced as worn/used plastic with possible compromised integrity

proof_requests: Clear, full-frame photo of the manufacturer/capacity plate and UN hazard rating sticker
Photo of all four cage corners and base pallet for rust/damage
Short video of the valve opening and liquid flow test
Any paperwork or label showing the tank's last stored product
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable as a used caged IBC tote of likely 1000L size, but all suitability and condition claims are unverifiable from the photos, so it must be priced at worst-case used/unverified-safety condition pending the requested proof.
